name: LogSentinel
tagline: A pocket SOC: detect attacks hiding in your server logs
problem: Colleges and small businesses run web + SSH servers with zero security monitoring.
Commercial SIEMs are costly, cloud-tied and complex to operate.
Brute force, SQLi and scans sit in logs that nobody ever reads.
By the time a breach is noticed, the attacker is already inside.

stats.label: false positives on a benign-only log (measured)
attacks detected in the demo (11/11, measured)
log lines/sec parsed on a laptop (approx.)

solution: Auto-detects Apache/Nginx, auth.log and firewall logs; robust to bad lines.
Signatures + sliding-window correlation + statistical anomaly detection.
Every alert: evidence, MITRE ATT&CK mapping and a response playbook.
Groups alerts into incidents with a kill-chain timeline; exports a blocklist.

features.title: Three-layer engine
features.desc: Signatures, stateful correlation and EWMA anomaly - all from scratch

features.title: MITRE ATT&CK
features.desc: Each alert maps to a technique ID with a why-it-fired note

features.title: Incident timelines
features.desc: Alerts from one IP merged into a kill-chain story

features.title: Live tail replay
features.desc: Streams the log at speed, lighting up attacks as they land

features.title: Bring your own log
features.desc: Paste or upload a real log; format auto-detected per line

architecture: Parsers -> normalize web/SSH/firewall lines into one event type
Signatures -> URL-decode then regex for SQLi/XSS/traversal/scanners
Correlation -> sliding windows: brute force, spraying, compromise, scans
Anomaly -> per-IP EWMA + z-score on request rate, UA/path novelty
Incidents -> group by IP+time into a kill-chain timeline
stdlib http.server -> JSON API + vanilla JS console dashboard
algorithms: URL-decoding signature matching - defeats percent/double-encoding evasion
Sliding-window correlation - N events in T seconds, distinct-key counts
EWMA mean + variance with z-score - per-IP request-rate anomalies
Credential-stuffing vs spraying - invalid-user ratio splits the two
Kill-chain incident grouping - phase-ordered timeline per source IP
tech: Python 3 standard library (http.server, re, urllib, datetime)
No pip, no CDN, no network - runs offline on a cheap laptop
Deterministic log generator with ground-truth labels for evaluation
innovation: Explainable by design - every alert shows evidence + the rule + MITRE why.
Three complementary detectors catch known AND novel attacks.
Ships its own labelled attack dataset, so accuracy is measured, not claimed.
Never touches your firewall - it hands you a blocklist to review and apply.
demo_flow: Open the dashboard - demo log is already analysed (12k lines, 16 alerts).
Overview: severity donut, top attacker IPs, requests/min with red anomaly markers.
Incidents: open INC for 192.0.2.77 - see stuffing -> compromise -> sudo kill-chain.
Alerts: filter to SQL Injection, open one, read decoded payload + MITRE + fix.
Live tail: hit Play - watch attacks light up in the streaming console.
Evaluation tab: 100% recall / precision, 0 benign FPs, throughput.
Export a blocklist, then Upload log to analyse a judge's own file.
impact: Free, offline security monitoring for orgs that can afford none.
Turns ignored logs into an early-warning system before a breach spreads.
Teaches SOC concepts (MITRE, kill-chain) - a learning tool for students.
No cloud, no data leaves the laptop - privacy and sovereignty by default.
business: Open-core: free self-hosted tool; paid support + managed rules for SMBs.
Campus/MSP tier: one install watches many hosts via shipped logs.
Rule packs and MITRE-aligned reports as a subscription add-on.
Near-zero running cost - stdlib Python, no infra to rent.
future: Live log tailing from files/journald instead of replay.
GeoIP and ASN enrichment for attacker context (offline DB).
Optional fail2ban/iptables apply with human approval.
More sources: IIS, Postfix, Windows Event Log, Kubernetes audit.
Tunable rule editor and alert suppression lists in the UI.
